chapter: Union, Emmett Hardy and Rampart Street Parade
title: Cornet players must play the lead; modern players compete
summary: A New Orleans cornet player has to play a proper lead, whereas today's players all try to cut each other.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: And, and, and, they, they went around and did some vaudeville tour with, with them. And, just like, just like, just like I say, I mean, uh, a conant has to, has to know, to, to play New Orleans type of music. You see, today, everybody tries to out, out, uh, do each other in a band. Mm-hmm. I don't know why. They don't, they don't, they don't, uh, don't get the feeling in, in a type of music that, that we all love to play. Mm-hmm. And Crosby bands, see, we all helped each other and say, just like, like the conant play, he's got to play the right kind of lead for that, for that voice chorus to let you know what the hell it is. You see what I mean? Mm-hmm. And after that one, when he starts playing, everybody plays their own chords, they play their own chords the way they want to, want to play it, see? Then they get back and get a ride out for the last. But today, I mean, everybody, I don't care whether, whether, whether he's a screecher or, or, or, or, or progressive guy or bebopper or whatever you want to call it. But, I mean, they all try and cut each other.

The conant player's trying to play more, more, more notes than a clarinet player can play. You understand? Mm-hmm. And all that, and, and, and, and the, the, the, the, the, the, the, the, the, the, the sound and stuff like that, you know?
That, that, that's just the way it is. I don't, I don't know any other way to explain it.
That's that, that's my version of it anyway.
